title: Vilasa 15. Jahnava at Kheturi and in Vrindavana
html:
Jahnava Devi, on her way to Vrindavana, stays four days at Kheturi and praises Narottama; her arrival in Vrindavana and meeting with Jiva, Gopala Bhatta and Lokanatha; the author on the command to write this book

1Glory, glory to Sri Chaitanya, glory to Nityananda!
Glory to Advaitachandra, glory to the devotees of Gaura!

2The name of Sri Jahnava Gosani is prema embodied;
has not Chaitanya's own shakti descended [to earth]?

3On her way to Vrindavana she came by that road;
hearing of it, Thakura Mahashaya rejoiced at heart.

4He and Ramachandra Kaviraja, the two of them, went out to meet her
and, coming to the Thakurani, beheld her.

5Humbly they praise her and bow down many times:
"Be merciful and come — this is your own home."

6The Thakura arrived [with her] at his own dwelling;
he serves her, joyful, smiling gently.

7The Thakurani herself, seeing Gaura-raya,
seeing his captivating beauty, wept.

8For four days the Thakurani stayed in that place;
every day ever new service was shown to her.

9How many provisions came — curd, flattened rice,
sugar, bananas, sweets — hundreds and hundreds of pots!

10Food of how many kinds came,
ghee, milk, pickles, and kasundi1 too.

11Four days of the joy of feasting, kirtana and a great festival;
he who saw it knows what he experienced.

12One night the Thakurani is sitting;
calling "Narottama!" she seated him close by.

13With her own hand she strokes his body;
what fragrance from his body — as of kunkuma and the like!

14"O Narottama, hear what is in my heart:
hearing of all your virtues, I longed [for you] with all my heart.

15In you I see all the conduct of a Vaishnava;
boundless is the joy of mind, ears and eyes.

16It seems to me that you are prema embodied;
truly your name is Thakura Mahashaya.

17Seeing the way you serve the Vaishnavas,
my heart was gladdened.

18Will there be such a day again, shall I see [you] once more?
Your bhava has filled my heart with wonder.

19What I heard from the lips of the Vaishnavas,
that I have seen with my eyes — and more, in every way.

20In Vrindavana you were named Thakura Mahashaya;
the Vaishnavas tell of all your ways of worship.

21The Vaishnavas came and told me;
that I would come here I told no one.

22I [alone] knew it, I said it — and Ramachandra knows;2
so too my eyes have found joy.

23Such service, such bhajana, such Vaishnava conduct —
who [else] in the three worlds acts so? I see no other.

24All these virtues of yours I shall sing everywhere —
in Vrindavana, in the land of Gauda, wherever I go.

25Gauranga is merciful — who can understand it?
What power, what mercy he puts into the heart!

26I have come to know that your body is a manifestation of prema;
coming and calling me, you have given me so much joy.3

27I have heard that Ramachandra is your inseparable companion;
in life and in death your companionship will not be broken.

28As I heard, so I have seen — boundless joy!
As is the guru, the Acharya, so is his disciple.

29Have mercy on me — may I reach Vrindavana happily
and see everything everywhere with a joyful heart.

30All those dear to Gauranga who are in Vrindavana
I long to see once with my eyes.

31Such a blessed day will come — I shall see Vrindavana,
I shall see Radha-kunda and Govardhana with my own eyes."

32The next day there was talk of the Thakurani's departure;
how many waves of separation arose then!

33They gave her a hundred coins for the expenses of the road;
for half a krosha they walk with her, weeping and weeping.

34After going a little way the Thakurani fell into thought;
seeing [this] with their eyes, both weep.

35Taking their hands, she says to the two: "Calm your minds;
go home, you two are my life.

36Worship Sri Krishna with my blessing;
[and may it be granted to me] to reach Vrindavana without hindrance."

37The Thakurani goes on her way with joy in her heart,
and the two, downcast, came home.

38So she goes on, road after road, along the royal highway;
after some days she reached Mathura.

39Having seen Krishna's birthplace and the place of Vishrama,4
the next day she goes on happily to Vrindavana.

40With her eyes she saw all the kunjas of Vrindavana
and felt herself fortunate.

41She came and stayed with Sri Jiva Gosani;
the Gosani bows down, deeming [it] his good fortune.

42All heard of the Thakurani's arrival;
everyone came to see her.

43Sri Gopala Bhatta Gosani and Lokanatha
came and, beholding her in person, bowed down.

44The Thakurani showed great affection to all,
[though] she did not know anyone's name, did not recognize anyone.

45Sri Jiva Gosani says to the Thakurani:
"Here is Gopala Bhatta, who came first;

46here, see, before you is Lokanatha Gosani:
by Chaitanya's command he dwells in this place."

47[They say:] "The Thakurani herself is the very form of Chaitanya;
you have mercifully granted us sight of you — we count it our good fortune."

48[The Thakurani says:] "I have come to Vrindavana by the strength of the Prabhu's command; may all of you likewise show me mercy.

49When there is your mercy, every perfection is attained —
I have heard it from the lips of sadhus; of this I am certain."

50The Thakurani says to Lokanatha Gosani:
"You whose disciple is Narottama are renowned in the world.

51I count myself blessed to have seen him;
such are his virtues — and on him is your mercy.

52What service of Krishna, what service of the Vaishnavas,
what righteous conduct, what establishing of dharma!

53In the three worlds I have not heard of nor seen anyone [like him];
seeing him, my heart was filled with great joy.

54It seems to me he is prema embodied;
not in vain is his name Thakura Mahashaya.

55Apart from you he knows nothing else in body or mind;
blessed in the three worlds is he who has such a servant."

56The Thakurani says to Gopala Bhatta:
"How wondrous are the ways of your disciple's disciple!

57Ramachandra and Narottama are one life;
seeing them both, my mind rejoiced.

58As is the disciple Srinivasa, so is his servant;
I have seen that all of them are worthy vessels, deliverers of the fallen."

59One with so many virtues, heard of from the Thakurani's own lips —
boundless is the joy of honouring them with praise.

60Having taken shelter at the feet of this Thakurani,
by her command I write, without fear.

61I write by the strength of the command — I have no understanding of my own;
again and again she told me to write all this.

62[I said:] "My only need is sadhana and remembrance;
what gain is there in leaving that and taking to description?

63Many faults come to light in description;
this happens, and moreover writing gives rise to disputes over doctrine.

64From this come offences; no one accepts [what is written]:
seeing what is written, they say otherwise of it.

65From this come offences," say the mahajanas.
[But] there is fear if one disregards the guru's command.

66If what I write should prove otherwise [than it should be],
let all the sadhus weigh it in their minds.

67Those of whom I write by the guru's command,
I know, all people praise when the truth is determined.

68Those who are dear to Gauranga, and those dear to them —
what their thoughts are cannot be understood.

69Let no one feel disbelief at this:
what I hear, that I write — such is my intent.

70And if anyone says: "This is not according to the shastras" —
mightiest of all is that in which the guru's command lies.

71If anyone does not accept these essential words —
I have no capacity to write this.

72He whose hope is the feet of Sri Jahnava and Virachandra,
Nityananda Dasa, tells the Prema-vilasa.

Thus ends the fifteenth vilasa of the Prema-vilasa.

Notes

  1. Kasundi, a Bengali mustard relish.
  2. The couplet is found only in the 1913 edition; the sense of the first line is unclear.
  3. A variant given in both editions: "drawing me here, you have caused [me] so much sorrow", i.e. apparently the sorrow of the coming separation.
  4. Vishrama ghat in Mathura.
